content:
If a POP account is set up as a deferred account otherwise commonly known as Global Inbox, then it only uses the folders in 'Local Folders'. It does not and should not be an account in it's own right with it's own folders in the Folder Pane. So, the 'Inbox' in 'Local Folders' is the Pop accounts Inbox. When you send an email, a Sent folder is auto created. When you compose and save as a Draft, then a 'Drafts' folder is created.

In Account Settings > Copies & Folders' for the Pop account, it should say for Sent, Drafts, etc to use 'Local Folders'. The same should be set for 'Spam Settings' - to use 'Spam in Local Folders.

If you have that set up, then it is working correctly.

IF you do not want to use Global Inbox (Local Folders), then you need to change all of the following:

  • Account Settings > Server Settings for pop account
  • click on 'Advanced' button
  • Select 'Inbox for this account'
  • click on 'OK'

Then reset all the other account settings:

  • click on 'Copies & Folders'
  • Select 'Place a copy in '
  • Select 'Sent folder on' and choose the pop account

Message Archives

  • Select 'keep message archives in '
  • Select 'Archives folder on ' and choose the pop account name

Drafts & Templates

  • Select 'Drafts folder on' and choose pop account name
  • Select 'Templates folder on' and choose pop account name

In left Pane Select 'Manage Spam'

  • Select 'Spam folder on' and choose pop account name

Then Exit Thunderbird wait a few moments, then restart Thunderbird.

Report on results

content:
Actually, I mislead you. After you create a new profile with the Profile Manager, you don't have to start Thunderbird with that profile like I said to do. It's enough to just create the new Profile which creates the folder into which you will copy the contents of your saved profile.

You can get an idea of when a profile was last used by the date stamp of many of the files inside the profile. For example. These are some of the files that are updated when I last closed or opened Thunderbird. You will have some of these, maybe not all:

storage.sqlite folderCache.json session.json virtualFolders.dat sessionCheckpoints.json cookies.sqlite cookies.sqlite-wal xulstore.json prefs.js global-messages-db.sqlite AlternateServices.bin webappsstore.sqlite-shm bounce-tracking-protection.sqlite logins.json favicons.sqlite-shm places.sqlite-shm

"%APPDATA%" is a system variable that stands for ""C:\Users\<your Windows login username>\AppData\Roaming\", so "%APPDATA%\Thunderbird\Profiles\" is the same as "C:\Users\<your Windows login username>\AppData\Roaming\Thunderbird\Profiles\". You can use either.

@Karina, I just remembered a similar discussion with a problem of failed reproduction of Umlaute in this forum at the beginning of the year. Unfortunately this forum doesn't allow a search going further back than a few weeks.

The user seeking for help was a German who received newsletters from a medical review in which Umlaute such as ä, ö et ü were not displayed correctly. We couldn't find the cause and eventually decided to continue via a remote control help.

If my memory hasn't failed since, the culprit was a setting in Settings > General > Language & Fonts > Customize fonts .... > Message font permissions: when we set a check mark at ✓"Allow incoming messages to use their own fonts" the Umlaute ä, ö et ü were suddenly displayed.
